title: For Loops with Vec
story: Your shopping app shows a list of items. You can't just print the Vec — you need to show each item on its own line with a nice format. How do you go through every item one at a time?
why: The `for` loop iterates over Vec naturally — no index variables, no bounds checking, just clean iteration over every element.
analogy: A for loop over a Vec is like flipping through a photo album — you see each photo one at a time, in order, without worrying about which page number you're on. When you reach the last page, you stop.
try_it: Create a Vec with 5 numbers. Use a for loop to print each number. Then add a counter variable outside the loop and increment it inside to number each item (1: apple, 2: banana...). Try iterating over an empty Vec — what happens? Create a Vec of Bool values and iterate over them — does each iteration move the Bool or copy it?
tips: The Vec is NOT consumed by the for loop — you can use it again after the loop ends
Use `for item in vec` when you only need to read items, not modify them
You can nest for loops: iterate over a Vec inside another for loop — each runs independently
common_mistakes: Trying to modify the Vec inside a for loop — you can't push/pop while iterating
Thinking the loop variable is an index — `for fruit in fruits` gives you the value, not 0, 1, 2
Using a for loop when you need the index — use a while loop with `.get()` for index-based access
